name: Commodity exporters minus finished-goods exporters (IMX)

origin.source_title: Commodity Trade and the Carry Trade: A Tale of Two Countries (Journal of Finance 72(6), 2629-2684)

how_it_works.simple: Countries that sell raw materials have riskier money than countries that sell finished goods. Buy the currencies of raw-material sellers and sell the currencies of finished-goods sellers.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a farmer and a baker: when hard times come, the farmer's income swings more, so you ask more to lend to the farmer.
how_it_works.precise: Signal = (net exports of basic goods + net imports of finished goods) / total trade, averaged over the prior four years. Long the highest-ranked currencies, short the lowest. Rankings update yearly; returns are monthly.

rule: Each year compute each country's trade ratio from the past four years of trade data. Long the top portfolio (commodity exporters), short the bottom portfolio (finished-goods exporters), equal weights, via forwards. Rebalance yearly, roll monthly.
data_needed: Bilateral trade by product type (UN Comtrade, free)
economic_rationale: Ready, Roussanov and Ward model commodity countries as more exposed to global productivity shocks, so their currencies earn a premium and also pay high interest.
why_it_might_fail: The return overlaps with carry. The sample ends in 2012, before the commodity bust of 2014-2016, and the commodity-currency link may have changed after 2020 (see RES-0001 on Rees, 2025).

reported_results.source: Ready, Roussanov and Ward (2017), NBER w19371, footnote and Table A-3
reported_results.market: Developed and emerging currencies vs USD
reported_results.notes: Quote: "which imply a Sharpe ratio for the IMX strategy of 0.42, as reported in the Data Appendix Table A-3" With bid and ask quotes. Annually rebalanced version with bid and ask quotes, NBER w19371 footnote citing Data Appendix Table A-3.

relevance.reason: Fits our commodity-currency hypothesis (HYP-0003) with free yearly data, but it overlaps with carry.

research.notes: Added from the paper library (RES-0010) on 2026-10-21.
